He played [[college basketball]] for [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]] and [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]]. ==Early life and high school career== Gomez attended [[Inglewood High School (California)|Inglewood High School]]. As a junior and senior, he earned Daily Breeze all-area honors. Gomez was a three-time All-Bay League selection as well as the league's Most Outstanding Player in 2015 and was named to the All-CIF Division I-AA Team in 2014.{{cite web |title=Terrell Gomez Joins Men’s Basketball Program |url=https://goaztecs.com/news/2020/4/20/terrell-gomez-joins-mens-basketball-program |website=[[San Diego State Aztecs]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=April 20, 2020}} He had scholarship offers from [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]] and [[Liberty Flames men's basketball|Liberty]], but both were rescinded when both schools had coaching changes.{{cite news |last1=Zeigler |first1=Mark |title=SDSU’s Terrell Gomez: little man, big game |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2020-12-06/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-terrell-gomez-csun-northridge-height-inglewood-high |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |date=December 6, 2020}} Gomez decided to attend Middlebrooks Academy as a [[postgraduate year|postgraduate]] student and took classes at [[East Los Angeles College]]. He committed to play college basketball for [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge]]. ==College career== Gomez averaged 11.7 points, 3.6 assists and 2.4 rebounds per game as a freshman. He was named [[Big West Conference|Big West]] Freshman of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Alexander |first1=Jim |title=Alexander: Terrell Gomez moves on, from CSUN to San Diego State |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/04/16/alexander-terrell-gomez-moves-on-from-csun-to-san-diego-state/ |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |date=April 16, 2020}} As a sophomore, Gomez averaged 19.2 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game. He was named to the First Team All-Big West.{{cite news |title=OSU men's basketball: Look at the opponent — Cal State Northridge |url=https://www.gazettetimes.com/sports/beavers-sports/basketball/osu-men-s-basketball-look-at-the-opponent-cal-state/article_f5b9dafa-936a-5c5d-b3bf-f62de0ae9fa5.html |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[Corvallis Gazette-Times]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On November 13, 2019, Gomez scored a career-high 33 points in a 94–82 loss to [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine]].{{cite news |title=Edwards brothers, Ross lead Pepperdine past CSUN 94-82 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401174413 |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 13, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 19.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game while shooting 43.9 percent from the field, 44 percent from three-point range, and a Division I-leading 94.8 percent from the free throw line.{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Tron |title=What does Terell Gomez bring to SDSU? |url=https://www.eastvillagetimes.com/what-does-terell-gomez-bring-to-sdsu/ |website=East Village Times |access-date=July 27, 2021}} Gomez joined teammate [[Lamine Diane]] on the First Team All-Big West, becoming the first pair of Cal State Northridge players to be named to the first team twice.{{cite news |last1=Soto |first1=Andres |title=Terrell Gomez enters transfer portal |url=https://sundial.csun.edu/157110/sports/terrell-gomez-enters-transfer-portal/ |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=Daily Sundial |date=April 4, 2020}} He transferred to [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] for his senior season.{{cite news |title=SDSU Hoops Picks Up Terrell Gomez, Transferring from Northridge |url=https://timesofsandiego.com/sports/2020/04/25/san-diego-state-hoops-picks-up-terrell-gomez-a-transfer-from-northridge/ |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[Times of San Diego]] |date=April 25, 2020}} As a senior, Gomez averaged 8.6 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game. He declined to take the NCAA's granting of an additional year of eligibility, instead opting to turn professional.{{cite news |last1=Zeigler |first1=Mark |title=Terrell Gomez won’t return to Aztecs next season |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2021-03-23/san-diego-state-sdsu-aztecs-basketball-terrell-gomez-return-turn-pro-csun-transfer-portal |access-date=July 27, 2021 |work=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |date=March 23, 2021}} ==Professional career== On July 13, 2021, Gomez signed his first professional contract with [[Final Gençlik]] of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Gomez's pro career starts at Final Spor |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/694058/Gomezs-pro-career-starts-at-Final-Spor |website=Eurobasket |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=July 13, 2021}} He averaged 21.6 points, 3.8 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game. On February 22, 2022, Gomez signed with [[JDA Dijon Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]] and the [[Basketball Champions League]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Dijon inks Terrell Gomez |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Basketball-Champions-League/news/732660/Dijon-inks-Terrell-Gomez |website=Eurobasket |access-date=February 22, 2022 |date=February 22, 2022}} On July 19, 2023, he signed with [[Hamburg Towers]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamburgtowers.de/news/franzoesischer-meister-uebernimmt-den-aufbau/|title=Französischer Meister übernimmt den Aufbau|last=|first=|date=July 19, 2023|website=hamburgtowers.de|publisher=Sportando|language=de|access-date=August 12, 2023}} On June 1, 2024, he signed with [[Chorale Roanne Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.chorale-roanne.com/terrell-gomez-premiere-recrue-choralienne/|title=Terrell Gomez première recrue choralienne|last=|first=|date=June 1,
